content.text:
## Investigation summary

**Bottom line:** This is a latency incident, not an error incident. There is one root-cause fault domain: the `ts.orders_other` data path used by `ts-order-other-service`, which is backed by `mysql-0`. Slow queries there propagate up through `ts-admin-order-service` and `ts-seat-service` to the user-facing `ts-ui-dashboard`.

### Affected endpoints and services (abnormal vs. normal)

| Service / endpoint | Abnormal avg | Normal avg | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ts-admin-order-service `GET /adminorder` | ~587 ms (p95 ~1.5 s) | ~15 ms | Calls order-other; the delay is fully in the child |
| ts-admin-order-service `POST /adminorder` | ~112 ms (p95 ~500 ms) | ~11 ms | Calls order-other `addcreateNewOrder` (~380 ms) |
| ts-order-other-service `GET /orderOther` | ~677 ms (p95 ~2.3 s) | ~4 ms | Dominated by `OrderOtherRepository.findAll` |
| ts-order-other-service `/refresh`, `/tickets`, `DELETE` | ~58–475 ms | ~3–5 ms | Same DB path |
| ts-seat-service `POST /seats/left_tickets` | ~48 ms (p95 ~220 ms) | ~8 ms | Its outbound POST to order-other is ~43 ms vs ~3 ms |
| ts-ui-dashboard (entry for admin pages) | ~33 ms | ~21 ms | Mostly propagated from the calls above |

No service shows a new 5xx or error-status pattern. Error counts are the same in both datasets.

Travel-plan and route-plan show small shifts that fall within normal variance, so I ruled them out.

### Origin

- `ts-order-other-service`'s own DB-facing spans are where the time goes:
  - `SELECT other.entity.Order`: ~115 ms avg vs. 0.72 ms normal.
